title: Multi-agent Workflows

body.text: — the main agent plans and dispatches subtasks to child agents, e.g. one searches the code, another writes tests, then results are combined back.

example: "'Do a security review of the whole project' → split into 3 agents: check auth, check the API, check dependencies — faster than one at a time"

title: When to split into agents

body.text: subtasks are independent and use a lot of context
— like searching across many files; each agent has its own context, so it doesn't crowd the main task's memory.

example: "A single continuous task, like fixing one bug → no need to split; doing it directly is faster"

options.text: Child agents that take subtasks to do in parallel
Independent subtasks, like checking multiple zones at once

question: What's the context advantage of subagents?

options.text: Each has its own context, not crowding the main task
They have no context at all

question: When should you split work into multi-agent?

options.text: When the work is big and splits into parts that can run in parallel

question: What do multi-agent workflows help with?

options.text: Distributing complex work so it's more manageable
